source: OECD (2025), Health at a Glance 2025: OECD Indicators, OECD Publishing, Paris
framing: Gap framing: every figure is what is NOT covered, NOT satisfied or unmet. Gap figures are 100 minus the published figure.
rule: HAL may phrase these facts freely but must not state any figure, ranking or claim that is not in this list. Verbatim report sentences may name other countries; only what they say about this country may be used.

facts.text: 14% of people in Luxembourg were NOT satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare where they live in 2024, versus an OECD average of 36%; satisfaction has deteriorated over the past decade.
14.4% of health spending in Luxembourg was NOT covered by government or compulsory insurance schemes in 2023, versus an OECD average of 24.9%.
1% of people in Luxembourg reported unmet medical care needs due to cost, distance or waiting times in 2024 (average of 28 OECD countries: 3.4%).
6% of hospital care costs in Luxembourg were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 11% on average in the OECD.
12% of outpatient medical care costs in Luxembourg were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 22% on average in the OECD.
53% of dental care costs in Luxembourg were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 68% on average in the OECD.
26% of pharmaceutical costs in Luxembourg were NOT covered by public or compulsory schemes in 2023, versus 42% on average in the OECD.
The share was less than 2% in Poland, Luxembourg, Colombia and Türkiye, but stood above 5% in Switzerland, Korea and Chile (Figure 5.8).
In France, Germany, Luxembourg and Japan, more than three-quarters of spending was covered through a type of compulsory health insurance scheme.
By contrast, in France and Luxembourg, out-of-pocket spending accounted for less than 10% of total health expenditure.

In 2023, PHC represented 14% of all health spending on average across OECD countries, ranging from 10% or less in Switzerland, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and the Slovak Republic to around 20% in Lithuania, Estonia and Finland (Figure 7.16).
In Austria, Canada, Germany, France, Luxembourg and Switzerland, spending on general outpatient care was much lower overall, accounting for 4% or less of health spending.

Overall, every third health dollar was spent on ambulatory providers in Belgium, Mexico, Finland, Luxembourg and the United States but this share was below 20% in Türkiye, Greece and the Slovak Republic.
